summary: South Carolina Republican strategist Lee Atwater refined the racially coded Southern strategy, push polls and planted smears from the 1970s, ran George H. W. Bush's 1988 campaign behind the Willie Horton ad, and chaired the RNC before dying in 1991.

evidence.note: born February 1951 in Atlanta; family then moves to South Carolina
family lives near Strom Thurmond; long segment on his filibuster and segregationism
1972 Nixon get-out-the-vote drive in South Carolina launches his political career
host explains the Southern strategy and its role in party realignment
1980 push polls and planted press question smearing Tom Turnipseed's shock therapy
audio of the 1981 interview is played with repeated racial slurs
prison furlough programs, Willie Horton case and 1988 attack ad
aftermath: furloughs and parole curtailed nationwide after the ad
1989 R&B album with Isaac Hayes and B.B. King, Grammy nomination
collapse at a fundraiser, brain tumor diagnosis, death in 1991 at forty
legacy segment linking his tactics to Trump-era Republican politics

notes: Transcript says he collapsed in March 1991; he actually collapsed in March 1990 and died 29 March 1991 (host also says a year-long fight). Childhood death of his brother in boiling oil is described vividly, hence child-death. RNC chairmanship is a party post, so politician-official was not used; entertainer-artist reflects the recurring music thread.
